(1) `result:CORRECTED` is not a real value: `curriculum/source-freshness-format.md` line 40 defines the tag as `CORRECT` (present tense), never `CORRECTED` -- `grep -rn 'result:CORRECTED' curriculum/` returns only this one line and its cached expanded-view copy, zero occurrences of the real tag anywhere in this file. (2) even the real tag is gone: the two backing-block entries this note points at (argyris-schon, google-beyondprod) carried `result:CORRECT` at the prior pin and have since been re-verified and folded into `result:OK` (lines 109, 117) -- `grep -n 'result:CORRECT\b' curriculum/lectures/the-loop-half-filled.md` returns zero hits. Harm: this is exactly the case the dispatch preamble names -- a maintainer block must state what is TRUE NOW, not a diff it just recorded -- and this clause states neither: no entry ever carried the literal tag it names, and the state it gestures at (two open corrections) has already resolved into clean re-verified stamps that narrate their own fix inline ("Correction verified landed", lines 109 and 117). A future editor grepping for `result:CORRECTED` to find the two corrections will find nothing. Not the same defect the prior pass flagged here (that clause, "...this file used to carry were wrong," has already been cut) -- this is a new inaccuracy introduced in the same edit that fixed the old one.
